product_sources.title: EMA Yondelis product information
product_sources.publication_note: EMA product page lists update 20 July 2026.
product_sources.summary: STS use is after anthracyclines/ifosfamide fail or are unsuitable; efficacy evidence mainly concerns liposarcoma/leiomyosarcoma. Monotherapy is 1.5 mg/m² over 24 hours every three weeks. Dexamethasone 20 mg IV 30 minutes beforehand is required for antiemesis and apparent liver protection. Central access is strongly recommended. Important risks include low counts/sepsis, liver injury, nausea/fatigue, muscle breakdown with renal failure, cardiac dysfunction, capillary leak, allergy and extravasation necrosis. Check counts, liver tests and CPK weekly for two cycles, then at least once between treatments; assess renal function and cardiac function, with LVEF before treatment and every 2–3 months. Fever, marked muscle pain/weakness, dark or reduced urine, jaundice, unexplained swelling/faintness, breathlessness or line-site pain warrant prompt assessment. Review strong CYP 3 A 4 interactions, alcohol, hepatotoxic medicines and statins. G-CSF is permitted according to local practice rather than automatically mandated. Ovarian combination therapy uses different dose, infusion duration and renal criteria; do not reuse it as STS monotherapy.

product_sources.title: EMA Halaven product information
product_sources.publication_note: EMA product page lists update 11 October 2024. Initial document and official indexed safety sections were readable; subsequent full-document requests returned 429.
product_sources.summary: The sarcoma indication is unresectable liposarcoma after an anthracycline unless unsuitable. EU dosing uses eribulin base: 1.23 mg/m² on days 1/8 every 21 days over 2–5 minutes; publications often report equivalent 1.4 mg/m² mesilate. Low counts/sepsis, neuropathy, fatigue, nausea, bowel effects and hair loss require counselling. Counts are checked before each dose. Sensory/motor neuropathy may require delay/reduction. Assess QT risk, correct electrolyte abnormalities and consider ECG monitoring with cardiac disease, bradyarrhythmias or interacting medicines. Liver dysfunction increases severe neutropenia risk; renal/hepatic dose adjustment requires the regimen-specific table. Fever/unwellness needs urgent review; report new weakness/numbness before further dosing and promptly report palpitations/fainting. Antiemetic prophylaxis should be considered; G-CSF is clinician-selected. Breast-cancer eligibility and outcome figures do not describe the liposarcoma context. The publication's salt dose must never be entered as the EU base dose.

product_sources.title: EMA eribulin scientific conclusions on severe skin reactions
product_sources.summary: EMA concluded that reported severe skin reactions warranted adding Stevens–Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis to product information. Include urgent assessment of blistering/peeling rash or mucosal injury without implying common occurrence. This is a historical regulatory safety source, not a regimen-specific incidence estimate.

product_sources.title: EMA Caelyx pegylated liposomal product information
product_sources.publication_note: EMA product page lists update 24 April 2026.
product_sources.summary: Pegylated liposomes alter distribution/circulation; PLD is not interchangeable with conventional or other liposomal doxorubicin. Listed indications include breast/ovarian cancer, myeloma combination and AIDS-Kaposi; general STS is not listed. Kaposi uses 20 mg/m² every 2–3 weeks, distinct from 50 mg/m² every four weeks. Risks include hand–foot inflammation, mouth ulcers, low counts/infection, infusion reactions, cardiac injury (including delayed), lung inflammation, extravasation injury and rare secondary blood/oral cancers. Review lifetime anthracycline exposure; monitor cardiac function, counts before each dose, liver function, mouth and skin. AIDS-Kaposi has substantial marrow/opportunistic-infection concerns; breast/ovarian toxicity rates must not be copied. Report chest/throat tightness during infusion immediately; urgently report fever, breathlessness, painful blistered hands/feet or inability to drink. Persistent oral lesions warrant assessment. Avoid heat and tight pressure on hands/feet. Do not declare PLD heart-safe or omit cardiac risk. Routine pyridoxine/steroid hand–foot prophylaxis is not established by phaseIII evidence. The Kaposi infusion instructions differ from the breast/ovarian instructions.

product_sources.title: HPRA Vinblastine Sulfate 1 mg/ml SmPC, 11 April 2025
product_sources.summary: Vinblastine is intravenous only; wrong-route administration can be fatal. Marrow suppression is dose-limiting; leucocyte nadir is usually 5–10 days after dosing. Risks include infection/bleeding, constipation or ileus, mouth inflammation, nausea, neuropathy, jaw/muscle pain, hair loss and extravasation injury. Hearing/balance injury may be lasting; fertility impairment is reported. Liver dysfunction can increase nerve toxicity. Monitor counts, liver function, bowel function and nerve symptoms. Report fever, severe constipation with pain/vomiting or abdominal swelling, new weakness/numbness, hearing changes, and infusion-site pain immediately or promptly according to severity. Product adverse-event frequencies are largely unknown; avoid inventing percentages. Some cardiovascular events were reported with bleomycin/cisplatin combinations and should not be presented as established desmoid-regimen rates. Do not substitute vincristine/vinorelbine, their doses or their evidence. The precise desmoid dose and administration technique must come from NCCP 00554/local administration policy.

product_sources.title: HPRA Methotrexate Pfizer 50 mg/2 ml Injection SmPC, 10 April 2025
product_sources.summary: Methotrexate inhibits folate-dependent cell processes. Key risks are mouth/gut injury, marrow suppression/infection, liver injury including fibrosis, kidney injury/accumulation, pneumonitis at any dose, reproductive harm and rare lymphoproliferative or neurological toxicity. Check blood counts, liver/renal function and mouth/respiratory symptoms. Dehydration and impaired renal clearance increase toxicity. Fever, severe mouth ulcers/diarrhoea, persistent dry cough or breathlessness, jaundice, reduced urine or new neurological symptoms need prompt assessment. Review co-trimoxazole/trimethoprim, NSAIDs, interacting antibiotics, PPIs, folate supplements and nitrous oxide; patients should not start these without oncology/pharmacy review. Avoid alcohol. PPI interaction concern is especially prominent with high-dose methotrexate. Do not import osteosarcoma high-dose hydration, alkalinisation, drug-level or rescue schedules into low-dose desmoid treatment automatically. Nor should generic psoriasis/rheumatology monitoring intervals or folic-acid schedules replace the oncology regimen. The injected desmoid schedule must remain explicit; it is not a daily take-home dose.

evidence_sources.title: Demetri et al. trabectedin versus dacarbazine, phaseIII
evidence_sources.summary: Advanced liposarcoma/leiomyosarcoma after anthracycline and another systemic regimen. Trabectedin 1.5 mg/m² over 24 hours versus dacarbazine 1 g/m² every three weeks. Median PFS 4.2 versus 1.5 months; HR 0.55. This supports disease-control benefit in that selected previously treated population. It is not proof of cure, a universal STS result or an individual forecast.

evidence_sources.title: Patel et al. final overall-survival and histology analysis
evidence_sources.summary: Final median OS was 13.7 months with trabectedin versus 13.1 with dacarbazine (p=0.49). Disease control improved but an OS improvement was not demonstrated. Post-study treatment may confound survival; this does not justify claiming an established OS gain.

evidence_sources.title: Pautier et al. doxorubicin–trabectedin with maintenance, LMS04
evidence_sources.summary: First-line combination induction followed by trabectedin maintenance improved OS/PFS versus doxorubicin alone in metastatic or unresectable uterine/soft-tissue leiomyosarcoma. This is a distinct treatment strategy and population from NCCP 00374 later-line single-agent trabectedin. Do not attach its 33-versus 24-month OS figures to 00374 or imply that maintenance alone caused the benefit.

evidence_sources.title: Schöffski et al. eribulin versus dacarbazine phaseIII
evidence_sources.summary: 452 adults with advanced liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after at least two systemic regimens, including an anthracycline, were randomised. Eribulin mesilate 1.4 mg/m² days 1/8 every 21 days was compared with investigator-selected dacarbazine 850/1000/1200 mg/m². Overall median OS 13.5 versus 11.5 months (HR 0.77). This pooled result should not be treated as evidence of benefit for every sarcoma subtype.

evidence_sources.title: Demetri et al. prespecified liposarcoma subgroup analysis
evidence_sources.summary: Advanced dedifferentiated, myxoid/round-cell or pleomorphic liposarcoma, after at least two systemic regimens. Eribulin versus dacarbazine median OS 15.6 versus 8.4 months (HR 0.51;95% CI 0.35–0.75); PFS 2.9 versus 1.7 months. Keep the subgroup, previous-treatment and histology qualifications visible. The licensed liposarcoma indication is broader than the trial's minimum two prior regimens; distinguish authorisation from trial eligibility. Breast EMBRACE results and leiomyosarcoma results are separate. These medians are not individual prognosis estimates.

evidence_sources.title: Judson et al. EORTC PLD versus conventional doxorubicin phaseII
evidence_sources.summary: 94 eligible advanced STS patients:50 received PLD 50 mg/m² over one hour every four weeks;44 received conventional doxorubicin 75 mg/m² every three weeks. Response rates were 10% versus 9%. PLD produced less severe neutropenia/alopecia but more hand–foot toxicity. This is direct STS evidence for the 50 mg/q 28 schedule, but an old small phaseII trial with a substantial GIST component. Do not turn similar observed response rates into proven modern noninferiority, OS benefit or a treatment recommendation for GIST. Breast/ovarian efficacy studies do not establish the STS benefit.

evidence_sources.title: Stewart et al. PLD versus bleomycin/vincristine, phaseIII
evidence_sources.summary: 241 patients with HIV-related Kaposi sarcoma; PLD 20 mg/m² or bleomycin/vincristine every three weeks for six cycles. Response 58.7% versus 23.3%; PLD had more neutropenia/delays and less neuropathy. Direct schedule support for 20 mg/q 21, but a historical HIV-treatment context; not a current individual outcome forecast or general-STS evidence.

evidence_sources.title: Northfelt et al. PLD versus ABV, phaseIII
evidence_sources.summary: 258 patients with advanced AIDS-Kaposi received PLD 20 mg/m² or doxorubicin/bleomycin/vincristine every 14 days for six cycles. Response 45.9% versus 24.8%. This supports a separate 14-day schedule; label it explicitly rather than silently assigning its outcomes to 21-day treatment. Neither Kaposi study proves that chemotherapy replaces HIV-directed treatment.

evidence_sources.title: Azzarelli et al. methotrexate/vinblastine phaseII
evidence_sources.summary: 30 patients with advanced inoperable aggressive fibromatosis received methotrexate 30 mg/m² plus vinblastine 6 mg/m² weekly, median treatment one year. Partial responses 12/30 (40%);18 had stability/minor shrinkage with symptom relief; no complete responses. Small uncontrolled historical evidence supports local disease/symptom control, not a metastatic-cancer survival benefit. This 6 mg vinblastine schedule differs from DESMOPAZ and paediatric schedules.

evidence_sources.title: Toulmonde et al. DESMOPAZ phaseII
evidence_sources.summary: Non-comparative randomised open-label phaseII in adults with documented progressive desmoid tumours. Methotrexate 30 mg/m² plus vinblastine 5 mg/m² weekly for six months then fortnightly for six months;24 allocated, 20 assessable for activity. Six-month non-progression 45.0% (95% CI 23.1–68.5) in the chemotherapy activity group. Grade 3/4 neutropenia 45% and transaminitis 18% in its treated safety population. The chemotherapy endpoint was exploratory: do not claim a definitive head-to-head superiority result against pazopanib. Different vinblastine dose and schedule from Azzarelli; match NCCP 00554 before selecting quantitative evidence. Do not reuse the 2019 abstract's claim that no systemic therapy is approved as a current statement.

implementation_boundaries: Keep breast and liposarcoma evidence and eligibility separate within 00228; do not overwrite existing approved breast content.
Keep general STS 50mg/q 28 and AIDS-Kaposi 20mg/q 21 PLD profiles separate, including supportive care and blood-count decisions.
Confirm and explain off-label use from current NCCP/local policy; a regimen’s appearance in an Irish protocol does not itself alter the EU product licence.
Desmoid goals should concern local growth, symptoms and function. Do not use a generic metastatic sarcoma prognosis narrative.
No source safety frequency should be presented as this specific regimen's risk unless the population, dose, denominator and grading match.
Maintain generic chemotherapy consent plus agent-specific risks and urgent actions; these research summaries do not constitute complete consent forms.
retrieval_limitations: An older indexed methotrexate 1g SmPC URL returned 404; the verified 50mg/2ml April 2025 source replaces it.
EMA Halaven further full-text reads were rate-limited 429; initial dose/indication text and official indexed safety sections were usable. Do not claim every current table was visually inspected.
A ScienceDirect full article request was blocked 403; PLD STS primary abstract was read through indexed PubMed/publisher text. No repeated access-control workaround was attempted.
